accommodations.name: Immanuel Wilderness Lodge
accommodations.destination_text: Situated northeast of Windhoek in Central Namibia, the Eros Mountains neighbour the capital city of this spectacularly scenic country. The terrain is characterised by steep rocky ridges, vast valleys and sharp peaks. The Eros Mountains lie at an impressive 2000 metres above sea level, and those who are feeling adventurous can summit Ludwigkop Peak, the highest point of the range. Visitors can also enjoy a variety of activities such as horse riding. Commonly spotted wildlife include baboons, deer, a variety of bird species, and an array of other fascinating creatures.

information.description: Immanuel Wilderness Lodge, located just outside Windhoek in Namibia, offers a tranquil retreat in the savannah. Guests can choose from nine charming rooms equipped with modern amenities such as air conditioning, comfortable king-size beds, and private bathrooms. The property features facilities such as a restaurant, an outdoor swimming pool, and baggage storage. Activities available include visiting nearby attractions like Human Dreams Namibia and Okapuka Ranch.

accommodations.name: Otjiwa Collection - Thorn Bush Tented Camp
accommodations.destination_text: Set in the heart of Namibia’s Otjozondjupa region, Otjiwa Game Reserve spans 12,000 hectares of open bushveld, rolling plains and acacia-studded savanna. The reserve exudes a serene and private atmosphere, where wildlife roams freely, and the horizon stretches unbroken beneath vast African skies. Visitors can embark on guided game drives to spot giraffe, zebra, antelope and rhino, or enjoy walking safaris that reveal the subtle rhythms of the bush. At sunrise, the air carries the scent of dry grass and earth, while the calls of birds and distant wildlife punctuate the quiet, a place where Namibia’s wild beauty is both immersive and unforgettable.

rooms.name: Family Rooms
rooms.description: For families, two suites are designed with adjoining bedrooms and private bathrooms, providing ample space and comfort for all. The spacious tented suites are designed for ultimate comfort and privacy. Each suite features a private wooden deck overlooking the tranquil riverbed, allowing guests to relax and immerse themselves in the stunning surroundings. Enjoy the comfort of air-conditioning, a luxurious en-suite bathroom, and an outdoor shower where guests can embrace nature in the most serene way.

rooms.name: Twin Room
rooms.description: The spacious tented suites are designed for ultimate comfort and privacy. Each suite features a private wooden deck overlooking the tranquil riverbed, allowing guests to relax and immerse themselves in the stunning surroundings. Enjoy the comfort of air-conditioning, a luxurious en-suite bathroom, and an outdoor shower where clients can embrace nature in the most serene way.

activities.name: Rhino Tracking
activities.description: This adrenaline filled morning will give you an experience that will form part of you. Experience coming up close to the wild white Rhino and get a sense of these majestic animals.

activities.name: Game Drives
activities.description: This game drive offers the opportunity to spot 25 different animal species. After an adventurous couple of hours, you will end the drive on one of our scenic mountain tops.

activities.name: Horse riding
activities.description: Become one with nature, whilst roaming the plains of Otjiwa. Our professional guides will make you feel at ease on horseback.

activities.name: Bird-Watching
activities.description: This activity gives you the opportunity to explore nature on your own time. You will be dropped off at one of the look out points, with a snack basket and a radio. Once you are done, you just give the lodge a shout on the radio, and a guide will come get you.

activities.name: Spa Treatments
activities.description: After a hard day's adventuring, relax with a massage, either in the dedicated spa and wellness centre or in the privacy of your room.

activities.name: Ombo Village visit
activities.description: Experience the culture and history of the Herero tribe. The Otjiwa guide will transfer you to the village, where the local guide will take you through the history and evolution of their culture, including dress and architecture. Enjoy lunch before returning to the lodge

information.description: Otjiwa Thorn Bush Tented Camp offers an authentic, immersive safari experience where luxury and adventure come together in perfect harmony. Whether guests are seeking a peaceful retreat, an unforgettable family getaway, or an exciting adventure in the wild, Thorn Bush promises an experience that will stay with them long after their journey ends. The camp features 10 spacious tented suites designed for ultimate comfort and privacy. Each suite includes a private wooden deck overlooking the tranquil riverbed, allowing guests to relax and immerse themselves in the stunning surroundings. The suites are equipped with air-conditioning, luxurious en-suite bathrooms, and outdoor showers for a serene nature experience. For families, two suites are designed with adjoining bedrooms and private bathrooms, providing ample space and comfort for all. At Thorn Bush, adventure and nature await. Guests can track rhinos on foot with expert guides, embark on thrilling game drives through the savanna, or take guided night drives to see nocturnal wildlife, ensuring every moment is filled with excitement. For a more tranquil experience, guests can enjoy birdwatching, cultural tours to Ombu Village, horseback riding, and rejuvenating spa treatments.

accommodations.name: Onguma Trails Camp
accommodations.destination_text: Situated east of Etosha, bordering Fisher's Pan, Onguma Game Reserve is one of Namibia's best-kept secrets. The reserve offers visitors the opportunity to experience Africa in all her beauty and diversity. Onguma Game Reserve features over 35 480 hectares of protected land scattered with a variety of wildlife including plains game, black rhino, kudu, giraffe, zebra, lion, cheetah, leopard and more than 300 bird species. The seasonal rains attract thousands of migrating birds to the Fisher’s Pan wetland area. The neighbouring Etosha National Park is home to a rich array of wildlife, including 4 of the Big 5. Visitors can enjoy game drives, guided walks and rhino research drives within the private reserve as well as wildlife safaris into Etosha National Park to view abundant game in the largest national park in Namibia.

activities.name: Walking Trails
activities.description: Adventurous walking trails in Onguma’s pristine wilderness, with the chance of spotting four of the big five on foot. Experiencing the Namibian bush on foot allows you to connect with nature around you and is the best way to discover well-kept secrets. Our guided safari walks are led by experienced and qualified walking guides with rifles.

information.description: Located in a remote part of Onguma's private 35,480-hectare wilderness, Onguma Trails Camp offers an exciting adventure for those seeking an immersive walking safari and the chance to spot four of the Big Five on foot. Every step reveals the natural beauty of the Namibian bush, providing an opportunity to reconnect with nature over two nights and three days — or extend your stay to three nights and four days. Blending rustic charm with modern luxury, Onguma Trails Camp features just four meticulously designed glamping bell tents, each with its own ensuite outdoor bathroom. With a maximum capacity of eight guests, the camp ensures an intimate and exclusive atmosphere. Guests set out on guided walking trails through this pristine wilderness to uncover tracks, edible plants, and the secrets of the bush, all while experiencing the thrill of encountering wildlife up close, on foot. Walking safaris provide an authentic connection to nature and the landscape that vehicles simply cannot match. Onguma Trails Camp combines adventure with serenity, delivering a walking safari like no other.

accommodations.name: Etosha Safari Lodge Gondwana Collection Namibia
accommodations.destination_text: Located just south of the boundary of Etosha National Park in northwestern Namibia, Etosha South makes up the southern region of this wild paradise. The area is comprised of a collection of world class private game reserves. The national park can be accessed via the southern entrance at Andersson’s Gate. Visitors can catch a glimpse of a variety of wildlife including: lion, giraffe, elephant, white and black rhino, and a multitude of plains game. Popular activities include: enjoying an open 4x4 safari with an expert guide, half day or full day drives with the option of a picnic lunch with wine on the full day game drive.

rooms.name: Standard Twin Rooms
rooms.description: The rooms are located on a hillock, overlooking magnificent views, with Etosha National Park in the distance. Rooms have twin beds, en suite bathrooms (showers), and a small veranda. All rooms have air-conditioners and complimentary tea/coffee facilities.

rooms.name: Standard Family Rooms
rooms.description: The rooms are located on a hillock, overlooking magnificent views, with Etosha National Park in the distance. Rooms are open plan with four beds, en suite bathrooms (showers), and a small veranda. All rooms have air-conditioners and tea/coffee facilities.

activities.name: Full Day Game Drive into Etosha
activities.description: Enjoy an unforgettable full-day guided game drive into Etosha National Park, one of Africa’s premier wildlife destinations. Travelling in a safari vehicle, you’ll have excellent visibility and plenty of opportunities to observe the park’s diverse, free-roaming wildlife in their natural habitat. Accompanied by an experienced guide, explore vast salt pans, open savannahs, and busy waterholes where animals gather throughout the day. Keep an eye out for iconic species such as lions, elephants, giraffes, and a wide variety of antelope and birdlife. Your guide will share fascinating insights into the park’s ecosystems, animal behaviour, and tracking techniques, making the experience both educational and exciting. A light snack and refreshments are included, allowing you to stay comfortable as you spend the day immersed in nature. Please note that park entrance fees are excluded. This full-day safari is ideal for wildlife enthusiasts and photographers alike, offering a deeper and more rewarding exploration of Etosha’s spectacular landscapes and abundant wildlife. Departure: ± 30 minutes before sunrise Duration: ± 9 hours (full day)

activities.name: Half Day Game Drive into Etosha
activities.description: Experience the thrill of a half-day guided game drive into Etosha National Park in a safari vehicle, offering exceptional visibility and close encounters with nature. Led by a knowledgeable guide, this immersive journey takes you deep into one of Africa’s most iconic wildlife reserves, where vast salt pans and waterholes attract an incredible variety of animals. Keep your camera ready as you search for free-roaming wildlife, including lions, giraffes, elephants, and many other fascinating species in their natural habitat. Your guide will share insights into animal behavior, ecology, and the unique environment of the park, enriching your safari experience. Light snacks and refreshments are provided during the drive, allowing you to relax and fully enjoy your time in the wilderness. Please note that park entrance fees are excluded. This half-day adventure is perfect for both first-time visitors and seasoned safari enthusiasts, offering a memorable glimpse into Namibia’s remarkable wildlife and landscapes. AM Departure: ± 30 minutes before sunrise PM Departure: ± 14:00 (enquire at reception) Duration: ± 5 - 6 hours

activities.name: Guided Walk (2 - 3.5km)
activities.description: Start your day with a refreshing guided walk between Etosha Safari Lodge and Etosha Safari Camp, covering a distance of approximately 2 to 3.5 km. Led by an experienced guide, this leisurely walk offers a chance to immerse yourself in the sights, sounds, and scents of the African bush. Along the way, you’ll learn to spot animal tracks, identify native plants, and gain insight into the smaller details of the ecosystem that are often missed on game drives. Your guide will share fascinating stories about the area’s wildlife, geology, and cultural heritage, making the experience both educational and engaging. This walk is suitable for most fitness levels and is conducted at a relaxed pace, allowing plenty of time to pause, observe, and take in the surrounding landscape. Whether you’re a nature enthusiast or simply looking for a peaceful outdoor activity, this guided walk is the perfect way to connect with the environment on a more personal level. Departure: morning or afternoon (enquire at reception) Duration: ± 1 - 2 hours

activities.name: Self-Drive Safari through Etosha National Park
activities.description: Begin your self-drive safari into Etosha National Park from Anderson Gate, the park’s main entrance. From here, you can explore the park at your own pace, visiting key rest camps and waterholes such as Okaukuejo Camp, Halali Camp, and Namutoni Camp. Drive along well-marked roads through open savannahs, salt pans, and around active waterholes, where wildlife such as elephants, giraffes, lions, springboks, and many other species can often be seen. Each camp offers excellent facilities for rest, refreshments, and photography, making it easy to plan stops throughout the day. A self-drive safari gives you the flexibility to spend more time at busy waterholes or scenic viewpoints while observing animals in their natural habitat. Travel safely, follow park rules, and take advantage of designated picnic spots for a relaxing break. Park entrance fees are not included. This self-drive option from Anderson Gate provides a convenient and flexible way to experience Etosha’s iconic wildlife and landscapes, while exploring the park’s main camps and enjoying Namibia’s unique natural beauty at your own pace.

information.description: Sip on a drink while watching the ruby sun dip into the mopane woodland. Perched on a hill with expansive views, this stylish lodge offers 65 chalets that provide a peaceful base from which to explore the animal bounty of Etosha National Park. Location: 10 km south of Andersson Gate on the C 38 (Etosha National Park).

accommodations.name: Hoada Campsite
accommodations.destination_text: Palmwag is a nature reserve idyllically located along a palm-lined tributary of the Uniab River, halfway between Swakopmund and Etosha, providing an ideal base from which to see the sights of the Kunene region or embark on one of the many local hiking trails. Water is scarce in this area, so the river’s presence often lures elephants closer to the camps. The reserve is notable for its unusual species of palm tree, the hyphaene petersiana, and for being home to the largest population of southwestern black rhinos in Africa. Animal lovers can also get a peek at leopard, lion, cheetah, mountain zebra, Angolan giraffe, springbok, kudu, and African bush elephant.

rooms.name: Campsite
rooms.description: Currently, there are seven campsites & 1 group campsite, each with its own well equipped bathroom facilities including showers and toilettes. The Group campsite can take up to 14 guests and have male & female ablution facilities

activities.name: Damara Culture Tour
activities.description: Guests will be guided through surrounding conservancy farms on foot, visiting a couple of authentic homesteads of the Damara people which allows them with the exclusive opportunity to spend time with their hosts understanding their origins, cultures, traditions and their approach to human wildlife conflict farming within the harsh desert conditions. Damara Guided walks at Hoada Campsite.? Your guide will take you to local households to appreciate how those people of Bantu origins who are related to the Himba and Herero build houses, prepare their food, heal with traditional medicine and manufacture artefacts for sale. Get those comfortable shoes out as it is about an hours hike to the farm and another hour back. Depending on the time spent on the farm, you can expect to be back at your camp after 3 hours.

information.description: Hidden among large grey granite boulders and Mopani trees, Hoada Campsite offers travellers a serene home in the wilderness of Namibia. Accommodation includes six luxury campsites with ample designated areas for tents or vehicles with rooftop tents, and permanent tents are available for hire. Each campsite boasts its own braai area and kitchen facilities with running water. There are also ablution facilities, with flush toilets, hidden amongst the rocks.

accommodations.name: Etendeka Mountain Camp
accommodations.destination_text: Resting majestically in the heart of Namibia's Damaraland region, The Grootberg Plateau showcases stunning natural landscapes characterised by deep canyons, dramatic rock formations, and expansive vistas. The renowned Grootberg Pass winds through mountains, offering spellbinding views. On the drive, one may come across the Himba people, known for centuries-old livestock farming practices. Encounters along the Grootberg Pass may include purchasing handmade jewellery while supporting the community with donations. Despite its rugged terrain, Grootberg hosts diverse wildlife, including black rhinos, giraffes, and desert elephants, adapted to harsh desert conditions. Additional activities include walking trails, birdwatching, and Damara Cultural Tours. End the day with a 4x4 drive atop the flat plains of the Grootberg Plateau that leads to a jaw-dropping viewpoint and watch the sunset.

rooms.name: Twin tent
rooms.description: En-suite Meru tents fitted with 2 x 3/4 size beds, with open-air bucket shower.

rooms.name: Double tent
rooms.description: En-suite Meru tents fitted with 1 x double size bed, with an open-air bucket shower.

restaurants.name: Etendeka Dining Area
restaurants.description: Simple, fresh, wholesome meals are prepared, either in solar ovens or on open fires, and enjoyed under African skies. Extensive use is made of solar power throughout the camp. Etendeka is one of only two establishments that have been awarded the highest rank in the Namibian Eco-awards.

activities.name: Scenic- & Gameviewing Transfer to the Camp
activities.description: Arriving guests are met at the pickup point situated at Palmwag Lodge, where secure parking is provided, and transferred by game viewing vehicle the 18km to the camp. This limits the number of vehicles using the concession tracks. The transfer usually takes an hour and a half and provides an introduction to the area and the guide will explain briefly the geology, fauna and flora and some general details about the concession. Transfer Pick-up time: 16h00 (Summer & Winter)

activities.name: Self-guided Sundowner Walk
activities.description: A short self-guided ‘sundowner walk’ is an option in the afternoon after arrival at the camp where guests get the opportunity to walk up a hill behind the camp to get a better idea of the spectacular setting and location of the camp.

activities.name: Guided Morning Nature Walk
activities.description: The morning activity is a guided three to three and a half hour nature walk. The distance is between 4 and 6 km with lots of discussion and interpretation. Conservancies are an important subject with the value of the conservancy to the local communities being explained.

activities.name: Afternoon Scenic- & Game Drive
activities.description: The scenic drive in the afternoon allows guests to travel to other parts of the concession and to have a better opportunity to see the wide variety of animals that have adapted to this harsh environment. All activities are accompanied by a guide; vehicles are restricted to the regular tracks and walks follow routine paths.

activities.name: Stargazing
activities.description: After dinner your hosts, Dennis and Bonnie, will point out some of the more interesting constellations, stars and planets with the aid of a ‘star pointer’ and a telescope. With minimal light and air pollution in this area, star gazing is a treat to the eye.

information.description: In the foothills of the Grootberg massif, set amidst magnificent scenery and the ancient Etendeka lavas of northern Damaraland, the ten en-suite Meru tents have been refitted with luxury mattresses and 100% cotton linen. Necessary comforts have not been overlooked with the bathrooms also benefiting from a makeover, while the traditional, open-air bucket shower still holds pride of place. Simple, fresh, wholesome meals are prepared, either in solar ovens or on open fires, and enjoyed under African skies. Extensive use is made of solar power throughout the camp. Etendeka is one of only two establishments that have been awarded the highest rank in the Namibian Eco-awards. At Etendeka, wildlife has acclimatized to a precarious existence amongst the towering basalt mountains and dry mopane-shaded river courses of the Kunene Region. A strong focus is on walking activities. “The feel at Etendeka is rustic; we wanted to bring back that rugged element of the traditional tented camp that most have unfortunately lost.” Manager and co-owner of Etendeka Mountain Camp, Dennis Liebenberg has been running the property for the past 20 years and knows the area like the back of his hand. He loves to share his knowledge with guests.

accommodations.name: Mowani Campsite
accommodations.destination_text: Set in the Kunene Region of northwestern Namibia, Twyfelfontein is a spectacularly scenic area, featuring one of the largest and most important concentrations of rock art in Africa. The name ‘Twyfelfontein’ translates to ‘Fountain of Doubt’, which refers to the perennial spring situated in the impressive Huab Valley flanked by the slopes of a sandstone table mountain. It was this spring that attracted Stone Age hunters over six thousand years ago, and it was during this time that the extensive group of rock engravings and paintings were produced. Visitors can look forward to basing themselves at some wonderfully shady campsites along the Aba-Huab riverbed, while exploring over thirty different sacred ritual sites of the traditional hunter-gatherer communities.

rooms.name: Camping Site
rooms.description: Each camping site has offers sweeping views across Damaraland. Each campsite has its own private ablution facilities – shower, basin and toilet, along with a braai / BBQ, a kitchen wash-up area and shaded area with a seating bench. The campsites do not have electricity, however, are serviced on a daily basis and boilers are lit on request at check-in.

restaurants.name: Kiosk & Pool Area
restaurants.description: At Mowani Campsite there is a small kiosk next to the pool area. Here they sell wood, ice, cold drinks, braai (BBQ) packs and snacks. There is also Wi-Fi in this main area.

information.description: Mowani offers campers 9 stunning campsites, a reception with pool and Wi-Fi as well as a shop where you can buy wood, ice, meat, drinks and other amenities. Each individual campsite has its own bathroom facilities; hot water provided by a 'donkey', flushing toilets and private kitchen wash-up areas with electricity. All sites offer stunning views of the area.

accommodations.name: Spitzkoppe Rest Camp
accommodations.destination_text: Situated in Namibia’s desolate, awe-inspiring Namib Desert, between Usakos and Swakopmund and about two hours’ drive from Swakopmund, the Spitzkoppe are a group of bald granite peaks forming one of Namibia’s most recognizable and dramatic landmarks. These enormous towering domes are a mecca for hikers and mountaineers, from beginners interested in guided historic walks to professional climbers seeking an adrenaline boost. Numerous ancient rock paintings can be visited as part of a guided walking tour. The extreme, barren landscapes and striking rock formations create an excellent setting for photography.

information.description: Spitzkoppe Rest Camp in Namibia offers an exclusive desert escape where dramatic granite peaks frame a camp designed for both adventure and comfort. Guests sleep in spacious tents equipped with proper beds, ensuite bathrooms, lighting, and simple yet tasteful furnishings. Leisure facilities include a welcoming dining tent, a relaxed lounge area, and a campfire boma perfect for evenings beneath the stars. Optional activities range from guided bush walks and cultural excursions to exhilarating rock climbing and stargazing in one of the world’s clearest night skies. This setting blends raw wilderness with refined hospitality, appealing to travellers who value privacy, nature, and discovery.

accommodations.name: Greenfire Lodge Swakopmund
accommodations.destination_text: Set between the rolling dunes of the Namib Desert and the icy Atlantic coastline, Swakopmund is a relaxed seaside town in western Namibia known for its German colonial architecture, cool coastal climate, and adventurous spirit. Palm-lined streets, historic buildings, and ocean fog create an atmosphere unlike anywhere else in the country. Travellers visit for desert activities such as quad biking, sandboarding, and scenic flights over vast dunes and shipwreck-strewn shores. Cafés, bakeries, and small museums add to the town's laid-back charm, though the Atlantic waters are brisk rather than tropical. With its striking desert-meets-ocean setting and mix of adventure and history, Swakopmund is one of Namibia's most distinctive destinations.

information.description: Greenfire Swakopmund Lodge is centrally located and offers well appointed, en suite rooms, a courtyard, garden braai facilities, a bar and safe parking. The lodge is situated within walking distance of the region’s major attractions, main beach and restaurants. The lodge is located centrally in the bustling Namibian holiday mecca of Swakopmund. It is part of the thriving summer tourist route and is also situated on the doorstep of the famed Namibian desert.

accommodations.name: Dead Valley Lodge
accommodations.destination_text: Deep within Namibia’s Namib Desert, Sossusvlei is a striking landscape of towering red sand dunes, among the highest in the world, pale salt pans and immense open skies. Part of the Namib-Naukluft National Park, it has a remote, almost otherworldly atmosphere shaped by silence, shifting light and extreme desert conditions. Visitors can climb famous dunes such as Big Daddy or Dune 45 at sunrise, when the sand glows orange and shadows stretch dramatically across the valley floor. Nearby Deadvlei, with its blackened camel thorn trees standing against white clay and rust-coloured dunes, offers one of southern Africa’s most distinctive desert scenes. The dry heat, the soft crunch of sand underfoot and the vast sense of space create a powerful atmosphere, though early starts and challenging temperatures are part of exploring this remarkable region.

information.description: Dead Valley Lodge is situated inside the Namib-Naukluft Park, between Seriem and Elim Dune and near the Dead Valley at Sossusvlei, Namibia. The lodge offers luxury tented chalets with panoramic views of the Namib Desert's towering red sand dunes and mountain ranges. Guests can enjoy Namibian-style cuisine at the on-site restaurant, savour drinks at the bar, and unwind by the swimming pool. Additionally, guests have access to morning and afternoon game drives to Sossusvlei and Sesriem Canyons.

accommodations.name: Namibrand Family Hideout
accommodations.destination_text: Spanning an area of 172,200 hectares and encompassing four distinct ecosystems, the NamibRand Reserve of southern Namibia is among the largest privately owned game parks in Southern Africa. Founded to conserve the unique environment and wildlife species of the Namib Desert, the park’s mix of dunes, mountains, rocky outcrops, sandy flats, and gravel plains provides habitats for a diversity of mammals, including hyenas, jackals, foxes, antelopes, and various wild cats. A plethora of bird species, reptiles, insects, and frogs also have their home here, alongside an array of plant species. Discover the mysterious ‘fairy circles’, unexplained bare patches in the sand, or enjoy a night of sublime stargazing - having been named Africa’s first International Dark Sky Reserve, it is one of the least light-polluted areas in the world.

rooms.name: Farmhouse
rooms.description: Rustic yet comfortable self-catering fully-furnished & equipped renovated farmhouse. NamibRand Nature Reserve Park Fees charged per person per night are compulsory & must be selected under Extras. ** The Special package option includes Park Fees **

rooms.name: Camping
rooms.description: 2 exclusive campsites for up to 8 people each. Solar hot water, lighting. Bathroom ensuite. NamibRand Nature Reserve Park Fees charged per person per night must be selected under Extras.* The Special package option includes a discounted rate and Park Fees

rooms.name: Campsite Jupiter - deluxe camp
rooms.description: Campsite w/ wooden deck,roof&wind shelter. Bathroom ensuite. Solar hot water, lighting, charging facility, w/chair accessible. Park Fees charged per person per night must be selected under Extras.* The Special package option includes a discount&Park Fees

rooms.name: Self-catering house
rooms.description: A renovated farmhouse, fully equipped and furnished for up to 10 people in your group. Water hole for animals and birds at your doorstep. Situated on the NamibRand Nature Reserve. Private and comfortable.

rooms.name: Campsite
rooms.description: Two private and remote campsites, Orion and Venus, with ensuite wood and canvas ablutions. Hot shower and flush toilet. Situated on the NamibRand Nature Reserve. Each campsite can accommodate up to 8 people.

information.description: In 1999, Andreas and Mandy Brückner got the go-ahead to convert the deserted home of Karakul sheep farmers on the farm Stellarine into what is known as the NamibRand Family Hideout today. It is remotely situated in south-western Namibia , on the NamibRand Nature Reserve, one of Southern Africa ’s largest private nature reserves. Three private and secluded campsites Orion, Venus and Jupiter (opening March 2019). Pre-booking is essential. In addition to our daily rates, a daily per person Park Fee is compulsory for contribution to the conservation function of the NamibRand Nature Reserve. You are advised to book at least 2 nights as our facilities are over 16 kilometres off the main road C27.

accommodations.name: Namibgrens Guestfarm Camp Site
accommodations.destination_text: Lying east of the Namib-Naukluft Desert, in Central Namibia, the Gamsberg area is home to the majestic Gamberg Mountain, dubbed Namibia's 'table mountain'. This area is a mecca for 4x4 enthusiasts, who tackle the steep Gamsberg Pass, a gravel road cutting through the rugged terrain. It is Namibia's highest, longest and most scenic pass overlooking the beautiful Kuiseb River in the valley below. Visitors can enjoy superb stargazing opportunities as there is no light pollution, hike along the trails traversing the Gamsberg Mountain, which stands at an impressive elevation of 2347 metres above sea level; and explore the Gamsberg Nature Reserve, home to indigenous plant life and a variety of wildlife.

information.description: Located in Solitaire, Namibia, Namibgrens Guestfarm Camp Site offers guests a camping experience in tranquil surroundings. The establishment features 12 private campsites which come equipped with barbecue facilities and washbasins. Each campsite also has private open-air ablution facilities. Guests can cool off and enjoy a swim in the lovely rock pool which overlooks the stunning surrounding landscapes. Activities in the surrounding area include bird watching, hiking trails, 4x4 trails and excursions to Sossusvlei, Naukluft Park and Solitaire.

accommodations.name: Sandwerf
accommodations.destination_text: Encompassing the bustling capital city of Windhoek, and the laid-back seaside towns of Swakopmund and Walvis Bay, Central Namibia features an array of towns, deserts, and wildlife reserves. The landscape of this region is characterised by grasslands decorated with clusters of Acacia trees, between the Namib Desert to the west and the lush Kalahari to the east. Visitors can soak in the steaming waters of the Cross Barmen Hot Springs, view a wide variety of wildlife, and explore the untouched beauty of the beautiful Erongo Mountains with the breathtakingly beautiful Spitzkoppe, which offers some of the best stargazing opportunities in the country. Divers and snorkellers will enjoy the incredible marine life just off the coast of Walvis Bay. Art lovers should make sure to visit the little town of Okahandja, famous for its fine wood carving and vibrant markets.

information.description: Sandwerf offers guests both comfortable and tranquil accommodations in Namibia. All bungalows are spacious, infused with Sandwerf’s unique charm, and spaced far enough apart to provide a sense of privileged seclusion, making it an ideal escape from the modern bustle. The open-plan kitchen and lounge area create a warm and welcoming setting for conversation, ensuring everyone feels at home. The on-site restaurant offers a selection of delicious meals, including succulent game meat cooked over an open fire and home-grown vegetables. For leisure, guests can enjoy various activities such as hiking, cycling, and cooking classes.
